fact_text: The State Bank of Pakistan's monetary policy committee cut the policy rate by 50 basis points to 10.5% on 15 Dec 2025, a decision most analysts had not expected.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Before the decision, a viewer survey cited by the reporter had most analysts expecting the policy rate to be held at 11%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest called the cut a symbolic move, timed for the December-January window before inflation was expected to rise again from March 2026, after Ramadan.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest said headline inflation had run at about 5% over the previous five months and expected full-year FY26 inflation of 6.5% to 6.8%, possibly near 7%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The SBP was expected to see inflation rise in the second half of FY26 because of a low base effect, then return within its 5% to 7% target range in FY27.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: SBP FX reserves reached about $15.8 billion, above the $15.5 billion the SBP had expected for December, after an IMF tranche was received.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected SBP FX reserves to reach more than $17.5 billion over FY26, which he said would let the central bank manage outflows through inflows.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: An IMF tranche of $1.2 billion was received, which the guest said added comfort to the external position alongside the rise in reserves.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The cut was framed as a window of confidence from stable external indicators, firmer reserves and steady oil prices, rather than a change in the SBP's inflation assessment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Oil was quoted at about $60 to $65 per barrel, which the guest said helped keep the external deficit under control.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The US Federal Reserve had also cut rates, which the guest cited as one of the factors giving the SBP confidence to move.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The rupee was reported to have appreciated about 1.2% by the decision date, while the dollar was under pressure against other currencies.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest put the rupee at about 282 per dollar at the decision date and said a move to 286 to 287 would be quite manageable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest's personal view was that the rupee would trade around 286 to 288 per dollar by June 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest said a rupee depreciation of 1.5% to 2% over six months would be manageable and would help exporters and domestic growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Large-scale manufacturing grew about 4% in Q1 FY26, which the guest said justified lower interest rates to support growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected real interest rates to stay clearly positive after the cut, given his view of 5% to 7% inflation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected the policy rate to stay around 10.5% for about six months from the decision, with little room for further cuts once inflation rises.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Lower fixed-income yields were expected to push mutual funds with large fixed-income exposure to raise equity allocations, adding demand for stocks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected a positive, gradual market reaction to the surprise cut, with fixed-income assets less attractive relative to equities after the decision.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Banks holding long-term government bonds gain a revaluation benefit when yields fall, after the guest said yields had risen and hurt bond books in the prior one or two policy decisions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest said National Bank, Bank of Punjab and MCB still offered dividend yields in the 9% to 10% range at current prices.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest said UBL's bond book had an average maturity of about 8 to 10 years, so a rate cut could bring a significant revaluation gain.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected Meezan Bank to see a positive effect from the rate cut through its long-term bond positions.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest expected Habib Bank to see a positive effect from the rate cut because its bond positions were described as favourable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: The guest said National Bank had taken strong long-term bond positions and expected good outcomes from them after the cut.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Fauji Cement was described as highly leveraged, so lower rates could have a strongly positive effect on its financing costs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: D.G. Khan Cement was also named as a highly leveraged company that the guest expected to gain from lower interest rates.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)

fact_text: Cement makers as a group were described as cash-rich, so the rate cut was expected to matter most for the more leveraged cement companies.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Policy Rate Reduced to 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-15)
